column1: # CIRISVerify evidence registry — impl: tier (CIRISVerify#233 / CIRISConstitution#17)
# The spec-map the Constitution's check_claims.py resolves cross-repo
# impl:CIRISVerify pointers against. Verify is the most-cited repo in the CC
# evidence layer, so its own manifest gates that every cited symbol still
# resolves.
# Validated by tools/check_evidence.py — a moved or renamed symbol fails CI.
# Columns: cc_decimal <TAB> clm_name <TAB> repo <TAB> path#symbol <TAB> crate@version <TAB> span_sha256
# span_sha256 is the SHA-256 of the cited item's own source text (declaration
# keyword to its closing `}` or `;`; docs and attributes above it excluded). A
# body that changes under an unchanged name fails CI: re-read the claim, then
# record the new span with `python3 tools/check_evidence.py --update-hashes`.

# 6.1.8 N1 infrastructure admission (CIRISVerify#337): verify_founder_quorum counts
# M-of-N founders over a caller-supplied roster; head binding absent (it does not
# check that the roster is the one at the lineage head the row names).
# CC assigns these decimals; this manifest is the citation of verify's implementation.
# Shipped, tested verify surface with no CC identifier yet. Listed here so the
# Constitution can issue decimals against real implementations rather than
# against a proposal. The `UNASSIGNED` marker is not a decimal; tools/check_evidence.py
# still resolves the symbol, so these cannot rot while they wait.
# Proposed CLM names are suggestions, not claims.
# 2.6.1 verification order (CC 2.6.1.8, steps 6-8): read_row_statement checks, after the
